### 7.11 Scope 11 — Sécurité serveur

Faisable intégralement en `request` Playwright avec tokens par rôle. Échecs déjà prévisibles : confirmation notaire par l'agent (refus alors que la spec l'autorise), note de résultat non exigée, clôture de réclamation par le technicien, approbation sans documents, suppression de document sans garde de statut, création de type de bien avec min > max. `api_upload_requires_token_role_ownership_and_project_scope` : `api/File/upload` n'exige **que** l'authentification, sans rôle, propriété ni périmètre, donc 3 cas d'échec sur 4 attendus **[À CONFIRMER dans `UploadFilesCommand`]**.

## 8. Proposition d'infrastructure (à valider avant le Scope 1)

- `playwright.config.ts` à la racine avec `testDir: tests`, `baseURL: http://localhost:5173`. Projet `setup` (login UI par rôle, écriture dans `tests/.auth/<role>.json`, fichier ajouté au `.gitignore` des tests). Un projet par rôle : `admin`, `padmin`, `agent`, `agent-other`, `buyer`, `buyer-other`, `notary`, `tech`.

- Un fichier par scope (`tests/scope-01-roles.spec.ts`, …) et `tests/GAPS.md` initialisé à partir de la §7.

### Machines à états backend (référence pour les tests de transition)

- **Vente** (`SaleStateMachine`) : `Draft → PendingNotary | Confirmed | Cancelled` ; `PendingNotary → Confirmed | Cancelled` ; `Confirmed` et `Cancelled` terminaux. Éditable = `Draft | PendingNotary`.
- **Rendez-vous** (visite finale, livraison, notaire) : `Requested, Confirmed, RescheduleProposed, Rejected, Cancelled, Completed, NoShow, Superseded`.

- **Réclamation** (`ClaimStateMachine`) : `Submitted → UnderReview | Cancelled` ; `UnderReview → MoreInfoRequired | Assigned | Rejected` ; `MoreInfoRequired → UnderReview | Cancelled` ; `Assigned → InProgress` ; `InProgress → WaitingCustomer | Resolved` ; `WaitingCustomer → InProgress` ; `Resolved → InProgress | Closed`.

## 6. Handovers ou Deliveries : lequel porte la livraison ?

**Handovers porte le flux réel. Deliveries est un reliquat, mais il est toujours actif.**

|---|---|---|
| Entité | `HandoverAppointment` / `HandoverReport` / `Warranty` | `PropertyDelivery` (legacy, rattachée à `Sale`) |
| Préconditions | réservation `Sold` (donc vente confirmée) ; unité non `DELIVERED` ; pas de RDV bloquant | **aucune** (vérifie seulement que la vente existe et le périmètre) |

→ `no_duplicate_delivery_flow` **échouera** : les deux contrôleurs sont exposés et la route `/admin/deliveries` est au menu. C'est un constat à signaler, pas un `fixme`.

  - champs : `Field` rend un `<label>` qui enveloppe le contrôle, donc `getByLabel('Garantie (mois)')`, `getByLabel('Projet')`, `getByLabel('Immeuble')`, `getByLabel('Étage')`, `getByLabel('Type de bien')`, `getByLabel('Bien disponible')` **[À CONFIRMER à l'exécution, cas par cas]** ;
  - erreurs : `getByRole('alert')` ;
  - modales : titre (« Nouveau projet », « Créer une vente », « Modifier le projet »).
- **Zones sans sélecteur stable :**
  - lignes et cellules des `Table` maison (pas de `role="row"` nommé ni d'identifiant de ligne ; il faudra filtrer par texte, ce qui est fragile) ;
  - actions de ligne `RowActions` (menus d'icônes) ;
  - `StatCard` du dashboard (label et valeur sans liaison ARIA) ;
  - cartes du portail acheteur (`BuyerHandoverCard`, `BuyerFinalVisitReportCard`) ;
  - statuts affichés par `StatusBadge` (texte traduit, pas le code).
  → Ces zones justifieront une demande d'ajout de `data-testid`, scope par scope (règle 3).

### Machines à états backend (référence pour les tests de transition)
- **Réservation** (`ReservationStatus`) : `Draft(5)`, `Pending(0)`=SUBMITTED, `ChangesRequested(6)`, `Approved(1)`, `Rejected(2)`, `Cancelled(3)`, `Sold(4)`=CONVERTED, `Expired(7)`.
- **Unité** (`UnitCommercialStatus`) : `AVAILABLE`, `HOLD_PENDING_APPROVAL`, `RESERVED`, `CONTRACTED` (jamais produit), `SOLD`, `DELIVERED`, `SUSPENDED`, `CANCELLED`.
- **Vente** (`SaleStateMachine`) : `Draft → PendingNotary | Confirmed | Cancelled` ; `PendingNotary → Confirmed | Cancelled` ; `Confirmed` et `Cancelled` terminaux. Éditable = `Draft | PendingNotary`.
- **Rendez-vous** (visite finale, livraison, notaire) : `Requested, Confirmed, RescheduleProposed, Rejected, Cancelled, Completed, NoShow, Superseded`.
- **Résultat notaire** : `PURCHASE_COMPLETED, INCOMPLETE_FILE, BUYER_ABSENT, POSTPONED, NOT_COMPLETED_OTHER`.
- **Dossier visite finale** : `Open, RevisitRequired, ReadyForNotary, Closed` ; résultat du rapport : `CompliantNoSnag, CompliantMinorSnags, NonCompliantMajorSnags, NonCompliantBlockingSnags`.
- **Réclamation** (`ClaimStateMachine`) : `Submitted → UnderReview | Cancelled` ; `UnderReview → MoreInfoRequired | Assigned | Rejected` ; `MoreInfoRequired → UnderReview | Cancelled` ; `Assigned → InProgress` ; `InProgress → WaitingCustomer | Resolved` ; `WaitingCustomer → InProgress` ; `Resolved → InProgress | Closed`.

## 6. Handovers ou Deliveries : lequel porte la livraison ?

**Handovers porte le flux réel. Deliveries est un reliquat, mais il est toujours actif.**

| Critère | Handovers | Deliveries |
|---|---|---|
| Entité | `HandoverAppointment` / `HandoverReport` / `Warranty` | `PropertyDelivery` (legacy, rattachée à `Sale`) |
| Préconditions | réservation `Sold` (donc vente confirmée) ; unité non `DELIVERED` ; pas de RDV bloquant | **aucune** (vérifie seulement que la vente existe et le périmètre) |
| Effet métier | acquittement acheteur → unité `DELIVERED`, garantie créée à partir de `sale.WarrantyMonths`, contact `DeliveredOwner`, idempotent | statut texte libre, **aucun effet** sur l'unité ni la garantie |
| Frontend | `HandoverPanel` (réservations), `BuyerHandoverCard` (acheteur), `useUnitJourney` | `DeliveriesPage` sur `/admin/deliveries` : `deliveriesApi.list()` **renvoie `[]` en dur** (pas de GET côté backend) |

→ `no_duplicate_delivery_flow` **échouera** : les deux contrôleurs sont exposés et la route `/admin/deliveries` est au menu. C'est un constat à signaler, pas un `fixme`.

content.text:
I've finished Phase 0 and written the report to [tests/DISCOVERY.md](tests/DISCOVERY.md). I haven't written any tests or changed any application code.

## What blocks the start of Scope 1
1. **Playwright isn't ready.** Only `playwright-core` is installed (not `@playwright/test`), and no browsers are downloaded. May I add `@playwright/test` and install Chromium? That changes `package.json`.
2. **Test account passwords are nowhere in either repo.** The QA database has `e2e.{admin,agent,buyer,notary,tech}@qa.local` accounts, plus `gpia.padmin@test.local` for project admin. I need the passwords, or permission to create dedicated accounts through the API.
3. **The running APIs appear to use `GPIA_*_QA` on SQLEXPRESS**, not the LocalDB named in `appsettings.json`. I inferred this because the API returns 14 projects, the same count as that database. Can this database take test data? Nothing can be cleaned up, because most entities have no delete endpoint.
4. **Document uploads go to the real Azure account `stgpia1539`**, and the `documents` container they target doesn't exist.
5. **There is no "responsable technique" role** in either codebase. Which real role should the `tech_lead_*` tests use?
6. **The backend has no `SUR_PLAN` / `EN_LIVRAISON` / `FINALISE` statuses.** It derives them: `DRAFT`, `PLANNED` and `IN_PROGRESS` count as `SUR_PLAN`, `COMPLETED` as `EN_LIVRAISON`, `ARCHIVED` as `FINALISE`. Finalising at 100% actually produces `COMPLETED`, and no command ever writes `ARCHIVED`. Can you confirm this mapping?

## Main findings
- **Selectors:** the app has no `data-testid` at all. Buttons and labelled fields can be targeted by role and name. Table rows, row action menus, dashboard tiles and buyer cards have no stable selector.
- **Handovers vs Deliveries:** Handovers carries the real delivery flow: a sold reservation, buyer acknowledgement, then the unit becomes delivered and the warranty starts. Deliveries is a leftover with no rules, but it is still exposed, and `/admin/deliveries` always shows an empty list. `no_duplicate_delivery_flow` will fail.
- **Tests that should fail because the code breaks the spec:**
  - An agent can't confirm a notary appointment; only admins and notaries can.
  - The API doesn't require a note when the notary result isn't a completed purchase.
  - An assigned technician can close their own claim.
  - Approving a reservation doesn't re-check required documents.
  - Documents can be deleted whatever the reservation status.
  - A property type can be created with minimum area above maximum; only the update checks it.
  - The "Créer une vente" button ignores the project phase and final visit, which only the API checks.
  - Buyer pages call non-"mine" endpoints (sales, notary), plus one route that doesn't exist on the backend.
- **Features that don't exist yet (these become `test.fixme()`):**
  - A feature list on districts.
  - The spec's final-visit fields: feedback, reason, corrective action, follow-up.
  - Uploading documents while creating a reservation.
  - Cascading selects in the notary and claim forms.
  - Claim comments.
  - A default set of required documents.
  - Read-only mode on finalised projects.
  - Construction progress and delivered units on the dashboard.
- **Claim workflow:** the backend state machine differs from the spec's. It has an extra review step before assignment, several extra states, and no separate "validée" state. I need the mapping before writing `claim_workflow_follows_state_machine`.

I've added to my memory notes that the running stack uses the QA databases on SQLEXPRESS. I'll wait for your answers on points 1–6 and your approval of the report before starting Scope 1.

# Unit Journey

## Purpose

A single unit's commercial lifecycle assembled into five stages — reservation,
notaire, vente, livraison, SAV — shown at `/admin/units/:id` and embedded inside
the reservation detail modal.

The API has no "everything for this unit" endpoint, so the join is performed
client-side from list endpoints. `useUnitJourney` owns that assembly so both call
sites produce identical results.

## Backend endpoints consumed

Backend documents live in the separate backend repository; paths below are the
frontend's verified calls.

| Endpoint | Trigger and request | Response use |
|---|---|---|
| `GET ProjectAPI /api/Reservations/list` | `useUnitJourney`, `pageSize: 100` | Narrowed locally to `r.unitId === unitId`; the newest is the unit's reservation. |
| `GET ProjectAPI /api/NotaryAppointments` | Same `Promise.all`, `pageSize: 100` | Matched on `n.reservationId === reservation.id`. |
| `GET ProjectAPI /api/after-sales/claims` | Same `Promise.all`, `pageSize: 100`, wrapped in `.catch(() => ({ data: [] }))` | Filtered to `c.unitId === unitId`. |
| `GET ProjectAPI /api/sales/user/{userId}` | Only when the reservation has a `buyerId`; wrapped in try/catch | `summary.sales.find(s => s.unitId === unitId)`. |
| `GET ProjectAPI /api/Handovers/reservations/{id}/mine` | Only when a reservation exists; wrapped in try/catch | Delivery stage. |
| `GET ProjectAPI /api/Immeuble/{id}` and `/api/Immeuble/by-immeuble` | `UnitJourneyPage` resolving the unit from the route id | Unit record and its building. |
| `GET ProjectAPI /api/Immeuble` | Fallback when no building id is supplied, `pageSize: 100` | Scans buildings, fetching each one's units until the unit is found. |
| `GET ProjectAPI /api/construction/units/{unitId}/title` | Title card on the page | Land-title status and history. |
| `PATCH ProjectAPI /api/construction/units/{unitId}/title` | Title edit modal submit | Reloads the title card. |

## Components involved

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `features/journey/useUnitJourney.ts` | Fetches, joins and derives the five stages |
| `features/journey/JourneyStepper.tsx` | Horizontal stage indicator |
| `features/journey/JourneyTimeline.tsx` | Chronological detail per stage |
| `features/journey/UnitJourneyPage.tsx` | Route page: unit header, title card, payment schedule presence, journey |
| `features/reservations/ReservationsPage.tsx` | Second consumer, via `ReservationJourney` |

## State and data flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  H["useUnitJourney(unitId)"] --> PA["Promise.all"]
  PA --> R["GET /api/Reservations/list (pageSize 100)"]
  PA --> N["GET /api/NotaryAppointments (pageSize 100)"]
  PA --> C["GET /api/after-sales/claims (catch -> [])"]
  R --> F["filter unitId, take newest"]
  F --> S["GET /api/sales/user/{buyerId} (try/catch)"]
  F --> D["GET /api/Handovers/reservations/{id}/mine (try/catch)"]
  F & N & C & S & D --> B["buildStages()"]
  B --> ST[JourneyStepper]
  B --> TL[JourneyTimeline]
```

The hook holds `journey` as `UnitJourney | null` and resets it to `null` before
each run, so switching units shows the loading state rather than the previous
unit's data.

`buildStages` derives each stage's `StageState` (`todo` / `current` / `done` /
`blocked`) from what was found. Two status sets drive it:

- `DEAD_STATUSES` = `REJECTED`, `CANCELLED`, `EXPIRED` — the reservation ended
  rather than advanced;
- `IN_PROGRESS_STATUSES` = `DRAFT`, `SUBMITTED`, `CHANGES_REQUESTED` — still
  awaiting a decision.

`empty` is set when nothing at all has happened on the unit, so the UI can render
a single empty state instead of five `todo` stages.

`UnitJourneyPage` resolves the unit itself: if the query string supplies a
building id it fetches that building and its units directly; otherwise it lists
up to 100 buildings and fetches each one's units in turn until it finds the unit.

## UI behavior notes

- The claims call is deliberately tolerant: `claimsApi.list` is admin/technician
  only, so an agent viewing the journey gets a 403 that is caught and turned into
  an empty list rather than failing the whole `Promise.all`.
- The sales and handover lookups are likewise individually wrapped, so a missing
  sale or an unscheduled handover leaves that stage `todo` instead of erroring.
- The title card is editable in place; changing the status opens a small modal
  and re-reads afterwards.
- The same stepper and timeline render inside the reservation detail modal via
  `ReservationJourney`.

## Known edge cases

- Every join is done over a **single page of 100 rows**. A unit whose
  reservation, notary appointment or claim falls outside the first 100 of the
  respective list is shown as having none. There is no per-unit filter on those
  endpoints, and no paging loop here.
- `salesApi.getByUser` is keyed on the reservation's `buyerId`, so a walk-in
  buyer with no account never resolves a sale and the "vente" stage stays `todo`
  even after a notarial conversion.
- `handoversApi.getMyStatus` is reservation-scoped and its backend handler admits
  internal roles through the project perimeter, so an agent sees the delivery
  stage; a caller outside the perimeter gets a 403 that is caught and treated as
  "no delivery".
- The fallback unit lookup in `UnitJourneyPage` issues one request per building
  until it finds a match — up to 101 requests for a unit in the last building.
- The journey is assembled from five endpoints with no shared caching, and it is
  re-assembled independently each time the reservation modal opens.
- `notaryApi.listAppointments` is matched on `reservationId`; a unit whose
  reservation was superseded and re-created would match the newest reservation
  only.

import { defineConfig, devices } from "@playwright/test";
import { ROLE_PROJECTS } from "./tests/support/accounts";

/**
 * E2E suite for the Projet → Réservation → Vente → Livraison → SAV journey.
 *
 * One Playwright project per role: each loads that role's storageState and
 * runs only the tests tagged with it (`@agent`, `@buyer`, …), so a session
 * never leaks from one role to another. Cross-role preconditions are built
 * through the API by `tests/support/state.ts`, not by driving a second UI.
 *
 * Requires the stack to be running: Vite on 5173, AuthenticationAPI on 48988,
 * ProjectAPI on 48989 (see tests/README.md).
 */
export default defineConfig({

# Fixes — Users & roles

## TECH_LEAD role ("responsable technique") added
- **Files:** `src/AuthenticationAPI/src/Domain/ApplicationUser/Entities/RoleCodes.cs`, `src/ProjectAPI/src/Domain/Users/Entities/RoleCodes.cs`, `src/AuthenticationAPI/src/Api/Application/Users/Register/RegisterValidator.cs`, `src/ProjectAPI/src/Api/Application/Common/Security/RoleGroups.cs`
- **Wrong:** the spec's technical lead (assigns claims, validates closure) had no role; only TECHNICIAN existed, and it could do both.
- **Changed:** new code `TECH_LEAD` in `Assignable`, `Internal` and `MembershipRoles` (project-scoped through memberships). `RoleGroups.AdminsTechnicians` now includes it; new `RoleGroups.ClaimSupervisors` = admins + TECH_LEAD.

## Admin account creation crashed for a role that did not exist yet
- **Files:** `src/AuthenticationAPI/src/Api/Application/Users/CreateUserByAdmin/CreateUserByAdminHandler.cs`, `src/AuthenticationAPI/src/Api/Application/Internal/ProvisionInternalUser/ProvisionInternalUserHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** `new Role { Name, DisplayName }` has no `Id` (`IdentityRole<string>` does not generate one) → `InvalidOperationException: Unable to track an entity of type 'Role'`. In `CreateUserByAdmin` the user was saved *before* the role was created, so the failure left an account with no role and never provisioned in ProjectAPI.
- **Changed:** roles are created with `Id = Guid.NewGuid()`; in `CreateUserByAdmin` the role is ensured before the user is written.

# Fixes — After-sales claims

## Technician could assign, reject and close claims
- **Files:** `src/ProjectAPI/src/Api/Application/Sales/AfterSales/UpdateClaimStatus/UpdateClaimStatusHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** any TECHNICIAN assigned to a claim could move it to any state the state machine allowed, including `Closed` (validation of closure) and `Assigned`.
- **Changed:** supervisors (GLOBAL_ADMIN, PROJECT_ADMIN, TECH_LEAD) may apply any valid transition. A technician must be the assignee and may only target `InProgress`, `WaitingCustomer`, `Resolved`; anything else → 403 `UNAUTHORIZED`.

## Technical lead restricted like a technician when listing
- **Files:** `src/ProjectAPI/src/Api/Application/Sales/AfterSales/GetClaims/GetClaimsHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** the "assigned to me only" filter applied to anyone holding TECHNICIAN, even when also a supervisor.
- **Changed:** the filter applies only to technicians who are not TECH_LEAD / admin; supervisors see their project perimeter.

## Claim list did not expose the assignee
- **Files:** `GetClaims/AfterSaleClaimResponse.cs`, `GetClaims/GetClaimsHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** the SAV screen could not know whether the signed-in technician was the assignee, so it offered every action to everyone.
- **Changed:** `AssignedAgentId` added to the response.

# Fixes — Projects, quartiers, construction

## No way to reach FINALISE
- **Files:** `src/ProjectAPI/src/Api/Application/Construction/FinalizeProject/FinalizeProjectCommand.cs` (new), `src/ProjectAPI/src/Api/Controllers/ConstructionController.cs`, `Construction/CompleteProject/CompleteProjectCommand.cs`
- **Wrong:** the business phase FINALISE maps to `ARCHIVED`, but no command wrote `ARCHIVED`; `complete` could also be re-run on an archived project.
- **Changed:** two-step lifecycle. `POST /api/construction/projects/{id}/complete` (100 % → COMPLETED = EN_LIVRAISON), then new `POST /api/construction/projects/{id}/finalize` (Admins, in scope, explicit confirmation, phase must be EN_LIVRAISON, weighted progress 100 % unless GLOBAL_ADMIN derogation with reason) → ARCHIVED, audited as a ConstructionUpdate. `complete` refuses COMPLETED **and** ARCHIVED.

## Project edit could bypass the lifecycle gates
- **Files:** `Projects/UpdateProjects/UpdateProjectHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** only a move *to* COMPLETED was blocked. A PUT could write ARCHIVED directly, or move a COMPLETED/ARCHIVED project back to IN_PROGRESS (reopening reservations).
- **Changed:** a status change to ARCHIVED, or away from COMPLETED/ARCHIVED, is refused (409).

## Project admin locked out of the project they created
- **Files:** `Projects/CreateProjects/CreateProjectHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** a PROJECT_ADMIN could create a project, but no membership was written, so every later action on it failed the §6.4 perimeter check.
- **Changed:** when the creator is a PROJECT_ADMIN (not GLOBAL_ADMIN), an active PROJECT_ADMIN membership is created for them.

## Project deletion cascaded through business history
- **Files:** `Projects/RemoveProject/RemoveProjectHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** DELETE hard-deleted reservations and sales along with the project.
- **Changed:** refused (409) when any unit of the project carries a reservation or a sale; only a project with no commercial history can be deleted.

## Quartier could not be deleted
- **Files:** `Quartiers/DeleteQuartier/DeleteQuartierCommand.cs` (new), `Controllers/ProjectController.cs`
- **Wrong:** CRUD on quartiers was missing the D.
- **Changed:** `DELETE /api/Projects/quartiers/{id}` (Admins); refused (409) while a project references the quartier.

# Fixes — Error propagation (ProjectAPI)

## Refused access returned as HTTP 500
- **Files:** `src/ProjectAPI/src/Api/Controllers/SalesController.cs` (`GET /api/sales/user/{userId}`)
- **Wrong:** a `catch (Exception)` wrapped every error in a 500 `InternalServerError` — a buyer asking for another buyer's sales got a 500 whose message said "Vous n'avez pas accès à ce dossier".
- **Changed:** local catch removed; `BuyerScopeDenied` now reaches `ApiExceptionFilter` → 403 with a stable code.

## Immeuble list turned any error into a raw 400 string
- **Files:** `Controllers/ImmeubleController.cs` (`GET /api/Immeuble`)
- **Changed:** local catch removed; errors are typed problem responses from the filter.

## Delete handlers leaked exceptions/stack traces as 400, not-found as 400
- **Files:** `Application/Projects/RemoveProject/RemoveProjectHandler.cs`, `Application/Immeubles/DeleteImmeuble/DeleteImmeublesHandler.cs`, `Application/TypeBiens/DeleteTypeBien/DeleteTypeBienHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** unknown id → 400 "operation failed"; unexpected exceptions returned as 400 with `ex.ToString()` (full stack trace) in the body; type-de-bien "still associated" → 400 with a custom body the frontend could not read (`detail` missing).
- **Changed:** not found → `NotFoundException` (404); in-use → `BusinessRuleException` 409 `RESOURCE_IN_USE` with a French message; other exceptions propagate to the filter (500 + requestId, no stack trace).

## Foreign-key violations surfaced as 500
- **Files:** `Filters/ApiExceptionFilter.cs`, `Application/Common/Exceptions/BusinessErrorCodes.cs`
- **Wrong:** only unique-index violations (2601/2627) were translated; deleting a row still referenced (SQL 547) produced a generic 500.
- **Changed:** SQL 547 anywhere in the exception chain → 409 `RESOURCE_IN_USE` ("Cet élément est encore utilisé par d'autres données…"). Frontend `BusinessErrorCode` union gained `RESOURCE_IN_USE`.
EOF

## Lists silently truncated to their first page
- **Files:** `src/lib/pagination.ts` (new `allPages`), `features/projects/ProjectsListPage.tsx`, `features/reservations/ReservationsPage.tsx`, `features/notary/NotaryAppointmentsPage.tsx`, `features/claims/ClaimsPage.tsx`, `features/buyer/BuyerSavPage.tsx`, `features/buyer/BuyerFileDetailPage.tsx`, `features/assignments/AssignmentsPage.tsx`, `features/immeubles/ImmeublesListPage.tsx`, `features/journey/useUnitJourney.ts`, `features/journey/UnitJourneyPage.tsx`, `features/appointments/AppointmentsPage.tsx`, `features/appointments/CommercialVisitReportModal.tsx`, `features/feedback/FeedbackPage.tsx`

for p,name,typ in [("typebiens/TypeBiensPage.tsx","LayoutFields","TypeBien"),("quartiers/QuartiersPage.tsx","QuartierFields","Quartier")]:
    s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
    fn="render"+name
    old=f"  function {name}({{ value }}: {{ value?: {typ} }}) {{"
    assert s.count(old)==1
    s=s.replace(old, f"  // A render function, not a nested component: a component declared inside\n  // the page gets a new identity on every render, so React remounted the\n  // inputs (wiping what the user typed) whenever the list reloaded.\n  function {fn}(value?: {typ}) {{")
    s=s.replace(f"<{name} />", f"{{{fn}()}}").replace(f"<{name} value={{editing}} />", f"{{{fn}(editing)}}")
    open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
EOF
cd ../.. && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json 2>&1 | head -5; cat >> docs/fixes/Projects.md <<'EOF'

## Quartier / type-de-bien forms lost what the user typed
- **Files:** `src/features/quartiers/QuartiersPage.tsx`, `src/features/typebiens/TypeBiensPage.tsx`
- **Wrong:** the shared field blocks (`QuartierFields`, `LayoutFields`) were components declared inside the page component. Every page re-render (e.g. the list finishing loading while the modal is open) created a new component type, so React remounted the inputs and cleared them; "Créer" then did nothing (empty `required` field) with no message.
- **Changed:** turned into render functions (`renderQuartierFields()`, `renderLayoutFields()`), so the inputs keep their identity.
EOF

# Fixes — Pagination (ProjectAPI)

## GET /api/Projects paged twice and filtered the perimeter after paging
- **Files:** `src/ProjectAPI/src/Domain/Projects/Interfaces/IProjectRepository.cs`, `src/ProjectAPI/src/Infrastructure/Repositories/ProjectRepository.cs`, `src/ProjectAPI/src/Api/Application/Projects/GetAllProjects/GetAllProjectsHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** the repository applied `Skip/Take`; the handler then removed out-of-scope projects and applied `Skip/Take` again. Page 2 was always empty, `totalItems` was the size of the filtered page (an agent asking 5 rows got "4 in total"), and projects beyond the first global page were invisible to any scoped user. No ordering, so page contents were unstable.
- **Changed:** the repository takes the scope set, filters before paging, returns `(Items, TotalCount)` counted on the same filter, ordered by name then id. The handler no longer re-pages.

## Unstable page contents (no ORDER BY before Skip/Take)
- **Files:** `Appointments/GetAppointments`, `Feedbacks/GetFeedback`, `Immeubles/GetAllImmeubles`, `Notary/Appointments/GetNotaryAppointments`, `ProjectAssignments/GetAllProjectAssignments`, `ProjectMemberships/GetAllProjectMemberships`, `Projects/LikedProjects/GetLikedProjects`, `Purchases/GetUserPurchases`, `Quartiers/GetQuartiers`, `Reservations/GetReservations`, `Units/GetAllUnits`, `Units/GetUnitsByProjectId` (all `*Handler.cs` under `src/ProjectAPI/src/Api/Application`)
- **Wrong:** paging an unordered sequence: rows could repeat or disappear between pages.
- **Changed:** deterministic order before paging (dates descending or name/number ascending, then id).

## Units by building: wrong total
- **Files:** `Units/GetUnitsByProjectId/GetUnitsByProjectIdHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** `totalItems` was the count of the returned page, so clients never saw more than one page.
- **Changed:** total counted before paging.

## Paging parameters never validated
- **Files:** `Common/Behaviours/PaginationBehaviour.cs` (new), `DependencyInjection.cs`
- **Wrong:** `PageNumber=0` / negative `PageSize` reached `Skip(-n)` → 500; unbounded `PageSize` could load a whole table.
- **Changed:** MediatR behaviour for every query with `PageNumber`/`PageSize`: values < 1 → 422 with field errors; `PageSize` capped at 500 (echoed in the response).
EOF
cat >> "C:/Users/LEGION/Desktop/realestateFront/docs/fixes/Projects.md" <<'EOF'
  (Backend counterpart: `docs/fixes/Pagination.md` in the backend repo — the project list endpoint itself was double-paging.)
EOF

# Fixes — Reservations & documents (ProjectAPI)

## Approval ignored the required documents
- **Files:** `src/ProjectAPI/src/Api/Application/Reservations/ApproveReservation/ApproveReservationHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** only creation/submission checked the project checklist; a file whose piece was removed, or submitted before the project added a requirement, could be approved.
- **Changed:** approval calls `ReservationDocumentChecklist.EnsureSubmittableAsync` → 422 `MISSING_REQUIRED_DOCUMENT`.

## No default checklist
- **Files:** `Application/Projects/CreateProjects/CreateProjectHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** a new project required no document, so any file could be submitted bare.
- **Changed:** every new project is seeded with `CIN` (CIN ou passeport), `RESERVATION_CONTRACT` (contrat ou bulletin signé), `RESERVATION_PAYMENT_PROOF` (justificatif de paiement), all required and editable per project.

## Documents could be deleted at any status; not-found errors were 400/500
- **Files:** `Application/Common/Reservations/ReservationDocumentPolicy.cs` (new), `Reservations/UploadReservationDocument/UploadReservationDocumentHandler.cs`, `Reservations/DeleteReservationDocument/DeleteReservationDocumentHandler.cs`, `Controllers/ReservationsController.cs`
- **Wrong:** a piece could be removed from a submitted or approved file (the documents the decision relied on); unknown reservation on upload threw `KeyNotFoundException` (unmapped → 500); unknown document on delete → 400 text; empty upload → 400 text.
- **Changed:** add allowed unless REJECTED/CANCELLED/EXPIRED; delete only in DRAFT/CHANGES_REQUESTED (409 otherwise); unknown ids → 404; empty file → 422 with a `File` field error.

## Reservation list: status filtered client-side, no building filter
- **Files:** `Reservations/GetReservations/GetReservationsQuery.cs`, `GetReservationsHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** no `Status` parameter, so the console filtered one page on the client (matching rows on other pages were hidden); no way to filter by building.
- **Changed:** `Status` and `ImmeubleId` query parameters, applied before paging.

## Historical 403 on document upload
- Not reproducible with an in-scope agent (200). A 403 is still returned — correctly — to an agent without a membership on the reservation's project (`PROJECT_SCOPE_DENIED`). Covered by `document_upload_does_not_return_403`.
EOF
cat > "C:/Users/LEGION/Desktop/realestateFront/docs/fixes/Reservations.md" <<'EOF'
# Fixes — Reservations & documents (frontend)

## Reservation could be started on a project in delivery / finalised
- **Files:** `src/features/reservations/ReservationsPage.tsx`
- **Wrong:** the creation form listed every project; the API then refused with 409.
- **Changed:** only SUR_PLAN projects (DRAFT/PLANNED/IN_PROGRESS) are offered.

## Documents could not be attached at creation
- **Files:** `src/features/reservations/ReservationsPage.tsx`
- **Wrong:** the form had no document input; the agent had to create a draft, reopen it, upload, then submit.
- **Changed:** the form lists the chosen project's required pieces with a file input each. With files, the reservation is created as a draft, the files uploaded, then submitted (unless "brouillon" is ticked). If a later step fails, the draft is kept, the form closes and the exact error is shown on the list.

## Cascade order and orphan values
- **Files:** `src/features/reservations/ReservationsPage.tsx`
- **Wrong:** order was Projet → Immeuble → Type → Étage; changing the type did not reset the floor, which could leave a floor with no matching unit selected.
- **Changed:** Projet → Immeuble → Étage → Type → Bien; each change resets every level below; types are narrowed to the chosen floor.

## Document types could never satisfy a project requirement
- **Files:** `src/features/reservations/ReservationDocumentsPanel.tsx`
- **Wrong:** the type picker was a fixed list (Contract/CIN/Blueprint/Other) while the checklist matches the project's own codes (e.g. `RESERVATION_CONTRACT`): a piece uploaded from the UI never ticked a requirement other than an exact code match. Delete was offered at every status.
- **Changed:** the picker lists the project's requirement labels (defaulting to the first missing piece) plus "Autre document"; upload hidden on REJECTED/CANCELLED/EXPIRED; delete only on DRAFT/CHANGES_REQUESTED; errors rendered with `role="alert"`.

## List filters were not related and status filtering was page-local
- **Files:** `src/features/reservations/ReservationsPage.tsx`, `src/api/http/reservationsApi.ts`, `src/api/interfaces.ts`
- **Wrong:** only a project filter; status was filtered in the browser over the loaded page.
- **Changed:** dependent filters Projet → Immeuble (the building list follows the project and resets when it changes, disabled until a project is chosen); any filter change reloads immediately; status and building are sent to the API.
EOF

# Fixes — Sales (ProjectAPI)

## "Créer une vente" offered when the API would refuse it
- **Files:** `src/ProjectAPI/src/Api/Application/Sales/SaleDrafts/GetSaleEligibilityQuery.cs` (new), `Controllers/SalesController.cs`
- **Wrong:** the console could only guess from the reservation status; project phase, final visit and existing sale were checked only when the draft was posted.
- **Changed:** `GET /api/sales/eligibility/{reservationId}` (AdminsAgents, in scope) returns `{ canCreate, reasons[] }` with the same preconditions as `CreateSaleDraftHandler`.

## Sale did not say where it is
- **Files:** `SaleDrafts/SaleResponse.cs`, `GetSaleByReservationQuery.cs`, `CreateSaleDraftCommand.cs`, `UpdateSaleDraftCommand.cs`, `CancelSaleDraftCommand.cs`
- **Wrong:** the response had no project / building / floor / unit, required by the draft sale screen.
- **Changed:** `ProjectId/ProjectName`, `ImmeubleId/ImmeubleName`, `FloorName`, `UnitNumber` resolved by `SaleResponse.FromAsync` on every sale endpoint.

## PENDING_NOTARY was never reached
- **Files:** `Application/NotaryAppointments/UpdateNotaryAppointment/UpdateNotaryAppointmentHandler.cs`, `src/ProjectAPI/src/Domain/Sales/Entities/Sale.cs`
- **Wrong:** no code moved a sale to `PendingNotary`, so that state (and its editability) could not occur.
- **Changed:** confirming the dossier's notary appointment moves a Draft sale to PendingNotary; cancelled / rejected / no-show / superseded appointments, or a completed one with a non-purchase outcome, move it back to Draft (`PendingNotary → Draft` added to `SaleStateMachine`). Saved in the appointment's transaction.

## Cancelled reservation left its sale active
- **Files:** `Application/Reservations/CancelReservation/CancelReservationHandler.cs`
- **Wrong:** cancelling an approved reservation released the unit but kept its Draft/PendingNotary sale active, which kept `IX_Sales_ActivePerUnit` occupied and blocked the next buyer's sale on that unit.
- **Changed:** open sales of the reservation are cancelled in the same transaction (traced in the sale notes).
EOF

# Workflow — Buyer account activation by invitation

**Status: fully traced**, across both services. This is the only workflow in the
solution that crosses the ProjectAPI ↔ AuthenticationAPI boundary at runtime.

## Business purpose

A buyer can be recorded and approved without ever having a login — an agent
enters a walk-in on the reservation's own identity fields. Approval then issues a
single-use invitation so that person can set their own password and reach the
buyer portal. The system must never invent a password for them, and never create
a second CRM contact for someone it already knows.

Ownership is split deliberately: **ProjectAPI owns the invitation and the CRM
contact; AuthenticationAPI is the only service that ever calls
`UserManager.CreateAsync`.**

## Participants

| Layer | Component |
|---|---|
| Frontend | `features/auth/ActivateAccountPage.tsx` (route `/activate?token=…`) |
| Adapter | `api/http/invitationsApi.ts` |
| ProjectAPI | `ApproveReservationHandler`, `AccountInvitationService`, `InvitationsController`, `AcceptInvitationHandler`, `AuthenticationApiClient` |
| AuthenticationAPI | `InternalController`, `ProvisionInternalUserHandler` |
| Tables | `AccountInvitations`, `CrmContacts`, `Reservations` (ProjectAPI) · `AspNetUsers`, `AspNetRoles`, `AspNetUserRoles` (AuthenticationAPI) |

## Step-by-step trace

### 1 — Approval issues the token

Inside `ApproveReservationHandler`, **after** the approval transaction commits
(so a failure here never rolls back a real approval):

```
if (hasBuyerAccount)            → GrantBuyerRoleAsync(...)
else if (PrimaryContactId != null) → IssueInvitationAsync(...)
```
